A white woman in her 60s presented for facial rejuvenation. She had panfacial lipoatrophy and photodamaged skin, with a medical history of nasal basal cell carcinoma. She underwent fractional CO2 laser resurfacing and fat transfer to her temples, forehead, and midface. After 2 weeks, she reported wart-like lesions that developed on her face. The lesions were firm, verrucoid keratotic papules that were itchy and irritated, and did not respond to conservative treatment including hydrocortisone, mupirocin ointment, and topical crisaborole ointment.
Firm, verrucoid keratotic papules were noted on the face. The lesions were itchy and irritated.
